nodes.name: In situ oxidation
nodes.procedure: Cu(OH)2 nanorod arrays were grown on copper foam via in situ oxidation at room temperature.
nodes.source_text: Figure 1a delineated the three-stage synthesis... Initially, Cu(OH)2 nanorod arrays were grown on copper foam via in situ oxidation at room temperature.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal transformation
nodes.procedure: Subsequent hydrothermal treatment with Co2+ induced a topochemical transformation through etching and coprecipitation mechanisms, evolving the nanorods into 2D CuCo LDH nanosheets with hierarchical architecture.
nodes.source_text: Subsequent hydrothermal treatment with Co^{2+} induced a topochemical transformation through etching and coprecipitation mechanisms...

nodes.name: Electrochemical activation
nodes.procedure: The pre-catalyst was electrochemically activated via cyclic voltammetry (CV) by scanning in the potential range of 0.924 - 2.024 V versus RHE at a scan rate of 50 mV s^{-1} for up to 1000 cycles. This process induced a structural reconstruction through selective Cu leaching, transforming the pre-catalyst into the Act-CuCo LDH with crystalline-amorphous heterostructure.

nodes.source_text: Finally, the pre-catalyst was electrochemically activated via cyclic voltammetry (CV) by scanning in the potential range of 0.924 - 2.024 V versus RHE at a scan rate of 50 mV s^{-1} for up to 1000 cycles.

nodes.characterization_summary: CuCo LDH shows ordered nanosheet arrays morphology. Act-CuCo LDH exhibits noticeable surface roughening after CV activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1b revealed the ordered nanosheet arrays morphology of CuCo LDH... After CV activation, the surface of the nanosheets exhibited a noticeable roughening...

nodes.characterization_summary: CuCo LDH shows smooth surface. Act-CuCo LDH shows surface roughening consistent with SEM observations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1b revealed... the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image inset confirmed its smooth surface... consistent with the observations from both TEM and SEM images (Figure 1d and inset image).

nodes.characterization_summary: CuCo LDH displays lattice spacings of 0.259 and 0.262 nm matching (1-21) and (021) planes. Act-CuCo LDH exhibits crystalline-amorphous heterostructure with lattice spacings of 0.474, 0.262, and 0.149 nm corresponding to (020), (021), and (1-22) planes; amorphous regions account for ≈25.26% of total area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) (Figure 1c) displayed well defined lattice fringes... The distinct lattice spacings of 0.259 and 0.262 nm matched the (1-21) and (021) crystal phases... Act-CuCo LDH exhibited a crystalline-amorphous heterostructure... crystalline phase presented lattice spacing of 0.474, 0.262, and 0.149 nm...

nodes.characterization_summary: CuCo LDH shows clear SAED patterns confirming long-range crystallinity. Act-CuCo LDH shows diffuse SAED spots confirming composite phase formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: corresponding selected electron diffraction (SAED) patterns (Figure S3a, Supporting Information) was clear, confirming the long-range crystallinity... The diffuse SAED spots further confirmed the composite phase formation (Figure S3b, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: CuCo LDH shows homogeneous distribution of Co, Cu, and O elements on nanosheets (Figure S2). Act-CuCo LDH shows uniform spatial distributions of Co, Cu, and O throughout nanosheets confirming partial Cu retention (Figure 1f).
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS mappings (Figure S2, Supporting Information) demonstrated the homogeneous distribution of Co, Cu and O elements on entire nanosheets... The Co, Cu and O elements were uniform spatial distributions throughout the nanosheets (Figure 1f)...

nodes.characterization_summary: CuCo LDH nanosheet thickness ≈10.43 nm. Act-CuCo LDH thickness ≈13.49 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Statistical analysis revealed a remarkable thickness increment from ≈10.43 nm (CuCo LDH) to ≈13.49 nm (Act-CuCo LDH).

nodes.characterization_summary: CuCo LDH shows characteristic diffraction peaks of crystalline CuCo layered double hydroxide (PDF#97-000-5069). Act-CuCo LDH shows nearly unchanged peak positions but significantly decreased intensities indicating epitaxial amorphous CoOOH growth.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2a, the pre-catalyst CuCo LDH revealed that the characteristic diffraction peaks were assigned to the crystalline phase of CuCo layer double hydroxide (PDF#97-000-5069)... for Act-CuCo LDH, the peak positions remained nearly unchanged, but the peak intensities significantly decreased.

nodes.characterization_summary: CuCo LDH shows Cu-O at ≈407 cm⁻¹, Co-O at ≈737 cm⁻¹, and CO-OH bending at ≈502 cm⁻¹. After activation, new Co-O peaks of CoOOH appear at ≈463 and 657 cm⁻¹ indicating phase transition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As depicted in Figure 2b, for CuCo LDH, the absorption band at ≈407 and 737 cm⁻¹ was assigned to the stretching vibration of Cu-O and CO-O bonds... After activation, the new peaks belonged to CO-O in CoOOH appeared at ≈463 and 657 cm⁻¹...

nodes.characterization_summary: CuCo LDH and Act-CuCo LDH show Cu peaks at 850-890 eV and 560-660 eV confirming Cu presence. Co 2p₃/₂: CuCo LDH 781.0 eV (Co²⁺, -0.3 eV shift vs Co(OH)₂ 781.3 eV); Act-CuCo LDH shifts lower by 0.5 eV indicating CoOOH. Act-Co(OH)₂ shifts by 1.0 eV. O 1s: M-OH ~531.5 eV, H₂O ~533.0 eV, new M-O 529.6 eV post-activation; S_{M-O}/S_{M-OH} = 0.145 (Act-CuCo LDH) vs 0.236 (Act-Co(OH)₂).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2c displayed the full XPS spectra... both Act-CuCo LDH and CuCo LDH exhibited distinct Cu characteristic peaks... Detailed analysis of the Co 2p high-resolution spectra (Figure 2d)... Figure 2e demonstrated the high-resolution of O 1s spectra... Figure 2f showed that Act-Co(OH)₂ exhibited a higher ratio of 0.236 compared to 0.145...

nodes.characterization_summary: C_dl values: Act-CuCo LDH 20.15 mF cm⁻², CuCo LDH 4.16 mF cm⁻², Act-Co(OH)₂ lower value indicating ECSA increase due to Cu leaching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical double-layer capacitance (C_dl) measurements via cyclic voltammetry (Figure 3d) demonstrated that ActCuCo LDH displayed a significantly higher C_dl value (20.15 mF cm⁻²) than pristine CuCoLDH (4.16 mFcm⁻²)... In contrast, the lower C_dl value of Act-Co(OH)₂ indicated structural collapse...

nodes.characterization_summary: Act-CuCo LDH shows HAADF-STEM image with corresponding elemental mapping confirming uniform distribution of Co, Cu, and O elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM image and the corresponding element mapping of Co, Cu and O elements for Act-CuCo LDH.
